description: "What is the DNA sequence at [chr:start-end]" / "get the reference bases for [region] in hg38" / "pull the sequence around [variant position]" — AUTHORITATIVE reference DNA for a genomic interval from the UCSC assembly, returned as a plain base string with its GC content. Use it to check what the reference allele actually is at a position, to extract primer/probe context, or to pull a promoter or exon sequence. The assembly argument is required because the same coordinates return different bases in hg19 and hg38.

chrom.description: Chromosome in UCSC naming, e.g. "chr7", "chrX". The "chr" prefix is required.

end.description: End position, 0-based and EXCLUSIVE (so end - start = length in bases).

genome.description: REQUIRED. UCSC assembly ID — the genome build your coordinates are in. Human: "hg38" (= GRCh38, current) or "hg19" (= GRCh37, what most older papers, dbSNP dumps and clinical spreadsheets use). Mouse: "mm39"/"mm10". These are DIFFERENT coordinate systems: the same chrom/start/end is valid in every build, so a wrong build returns confident annotations for a different gene instead of an error. Call ucsc_genomes to list the assembly IDs for a species.

revComp.description: Return the reverse complement — for a gene on the minus strand, this is the sense strand. Default false.

start.description: Start position, 0-BASED and inclusive. The Genome Browser UI and most papers are 1-based, so subtract 1 from a position you copied out of the browser location box.
